_note: Deplorable acts against a town (systems/townCrimes.js; ui/actionMenu/townCrimes.js, opened from the town's Back Rooms). daysPerYear: the calendar. odds: the chance someone sees the deed — base per act, less stealthPerPoint per point of Stealth and the Underworld trait bonus, more per point of the realm's heat on you (heatPer) and by the town's size (size); of those who see, `named` share know your face (the rest saw a figure and may name you later, nameChance a week while the hunt runs). hunt: the town's search for the culprit (days it runs; while named and in the town the watch takes you: arrestChance a day). caught: what being named costs — prestige lost from the House, the lord's memory (lordDeed), the town's memory (npcMemory kinds), a rumour (gossip rumorTypes), heat (underworld crimes). well: poisoning the town's well — needs one of `means` (poison, or carrion: rotting meat thrown down); the first draught strikes `firstShare` of the residents with the flux (more with poison), and the well stays foul `foulDays`, striking `dailyShare` more each day (a town without a roster keeps an abstract sickness `share` that idles its hands). scare: a false plague scare — `cost` gold to the criers and beggars (into the town's purse); traders shun the town (`tradeFactor` on its trade links) for `days`, `fleeShare` of its people go to the nearest town till it passes (fewer mouths, the same stores: its prices fall); each day `exposeChance` the physicians find no plague and say so (none when the town truly is sick), and then `traceChance` (less per point of Stealth) the lie is traced to you. granary: burn the town's granary — needs one of `tinder`; `share` of the granary and of the market's grain and flour burn (`leanShare` in the lean weeks, when the stores are thin and it bites hardest); `spreadChance` the fire takes the street around it (a town fire, systems/townMemory.js); the crown then buys grain at `crownPremium` over the market for `wantDays`. hoard: buy up grain in a hungry town (a famine of the age, a dearth, or the lean weeks with thin stores) and hold it in a rented loft (`loftFee` a week, to the town): legal unless the crown has forbidden engrossing (the loft is thrown open, nothing paid); `spoil` of it rots a week; selling it back in a hungry town at `grudgeRatio` or more of what you paid earns the town's lasting grudge. lines: the prose.

wellDone: You tip {means} into {town}'s well and walk away before the bucket comes up again.
Under cover of the washing-day crowd, {means} goes down {town}'s well. By morning the water will taste of it.
wellSeen: A washerwoman at the trough looks up as you step back from the well. She saw something.
Someone in a doorway watched you at the well — you could not see their face. They could see yours, maybe.
wellNamed: {witness} saw you at the well, and knows who you are. The town will know by nightfall.
"That one! At the well!" {witness} is already shouting your name.
scareDone: Coin changes hands with criers and beggars: by evening half of {town} has heard a sailor died of the black buboes in the harbour inn.
You pay the town's gossips well. "Plague," they whisper in {town}, "plague at the tannery" — and the carters turn their wagons round.
scareNamed: {witness} saw you paying the criers, and knows your face. The lie has your name on it.
granaryDone: The granary of {town} goes up in the night. The roof falls in on the grain, and the smell of burnt bread hangs over the town for days.
Oil, a flint, and the dry thatch of {town}'s granary does the rest. By dawn the winter's bread is ash.
granarySpread: The fire jumps the lane and takes the houses beside the granary.
granaryNamed: {witness} saw you running from the granary as the flames went up, and knows who you are.
hunt: The folk of {town} are hunting whoever did it: the watch asks questions in every tavern.
exposed: The physicians of {town} find no plague after all: the scare was a lie, and the traders come back.
traced: The lie of the plague at {town} is traced to you: the criers you paid have talked.
arrested: The watch of {town}, told who poisoned their people, take you at the gate.
hoardSeized: The crown has forbidden engrossing: your loft in {town} is thrown open and its grain sold off at the market cross. You see nothing of it.
hoardGrudge: You sold {town} its own bread back at a famine price. They will not forget whose loft it came from.
